title: Dutch Population Relocation Networks
subtitle: Netherlands · 2011–2024
description: Explore reconstructed municipality-level relocation flows by year range and demographic stratum. Municipality colours show net relocation balance, while directed curves show the strongest origin–destination flows.
imageAlt: The Dutch Population Relocation Networks atlas, showing demographic controls and a map of municipal net relocation flows in the Netherlands.

title: Job-Home Networks in Spain
subtitle: Spain · 2022–2024
description: Explore Spain’s job–home networks across six workplace-attendance recurrence layers. Directed flows show residential-to-employment connections, while district colours reveal hybrid-work intensity, network outcomes, settlement context, and spatial heterogeneity.
imageAlt: Interactive atlas of hybrid-work and job–home networks in Spain, showing district-level measures and directed residential-to-employment flows across workplace-attendance recurrence layers.

title: Global AI Co-occurrence Network from News
subtitle: Global · 2016–2025
description: This network, derived from global news, represents preliminary data for an ongoing study on global AI cooperation and competition. Currently, the study is working to further identify differences in competition and cooperation and apply them to machine learning.
imageAlt: Interactive atlas of global AI co-occurrence network from news, aggregated into ADM1 spatial units.

title: ABM of Regional Mobility in Central Macedonia
subtitle: MOBI-TWIN · Interactive agent-based modelling · Greece · 2025–2035
description: An interactive agent-based modelling demonstration of regional mobility and population change in a pilot region - Central Macedonia. The browser-based model uses a synthetic population to explore how alternative transition scenarios, remote work, relocation behaviour, congestion, and social influence shape regional outcomes over time.

title: Power Network on Social Media
subtitle: Bell and Drum Tower Planning Controversy, Beijing · 2012–2014
description: An interactive visualisation of three anonymised Weibo forwarding networks formed during the Bell and Drum Tower planning controversy in Beijing. Users can switch between expert-, government-, and civil-society-initiated networks to explore community structure, interaction intensity, and node prominence.
imageAlt: Interactive visualisation of an anonymised expert-initiated Weibo forwarding network, with filtering controls on the left and a community-coloured network graph on the right.

title: Network of Informal Participation
subtitle: Mashi Street Protection Controversy, Enning Road, Guangzhou · 2012
description: An interactive temporal network visualisation of Weibo forwarding activity during the Mashi Street Protection Movement in Guangzhou’s Enning Road regeneration controversy. The atlas traces how the network developed over time and allows users to explore communities, ego networks, and the network positions of journalism and civil society actors.
imageAlt: Interactive temporal Weibo network of the Mashi Street Protection Movement in Guangzhou, with timeline and network controls on the left.
